title: Protocol Layering, the OSI Model and TCP/IP
titleBn: প্রোটোকল লেয়ারিং, OSI মডেল ও TCP/IP
topics: Protocol Layering, the OSI Model and TCP/IP
keyPoints: Two principles of protocol layering: each layer performs two opposite tasks; objects under each layer at both sites are identical (slide 4).
ISO is the organization; OSI is the model (slide 6).
Physical: bits hop to hop; data link: frames hop to hop; network: packets source host to destination host; transport: message process to process (slides 9–18).
Session: dialog control and synchronization; presentation: translation, compression, encryption; application: services to the user (slides 19–22).
Why OSI did not replace TCP/IP: late arrival, incompletely defined layers, insufficient performance (slide 30).
